IA-2025-HF2801.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Read first time, attached to SF 2508.
Introduced, placed on Ways and Means calendar.
Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.

IA-2025-HF2801.policyArea: business assistance, major economic growth attraction program, tax credits
IA-2025-HF2801.aiSummary: The bill would change Iowa’s major economic growth attraction program, which offers tax credits to some businesses for big investment projects. It would set new site rules, including a larger site size for some projects and a special tax credit for one eligible business in a rural county, which it defines as a county with 50,000 people or less. It would also change when credits can be claimed, allow some rural county credits to be transferred, and let the state or county seek repayment if a business breaks the program rules.

IA-2025-SCR104.title: A concurrent resolution to provide for adjournment sine die.

actions.text: Resolution filed, laid over under Rule 25.

IA-2025-SCR104.aiSummary: The resolution would set Friday, October 2, 2026, as the final adjournment of the 2026 First Extraordinary Session of the Iowa General Assembly. It affects the Senate and House, which would agree to end that session on that date.

IA-2025-SF378.title: A bill for an act relating to speed limits, including the speed limit range for which certain excessive speed violations cannot be considered for certain purposes and the default speed limit for all vehicular traffic, and making penalties applicable.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Message from House, with amendment S-5153.
Committee amendment H-8231 out of order.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.
Committee report, recommending amendment and passage.
Subcommittee reassigned: Jones, Gosa and Siegrist.
Read first time, referred to Transportation.

IA-2025-SF378.aiSummary: The law changes how some speeding tickets are counted for driver records, probation decisions, and car insurance rates. It raises the default speed limit for all vehicle traffic from 55 to 60 miles per hour, unless another speed limit applies, and expands the speed zones covered by the rule to 34 to 61 miles per hour. It also lets road agencies use temporary stickers or overlays on existing signs when posting the new speed limits, and it became law in Iowa as Chapter 1132.

IA-2025-SF2484.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations from the rebuild Iowa infrastructure fund, technology reinvestment fund, and renewable fuel infrastructure fund, providing for related matters including financial assistance eligibility for regional sports authority districts, department of health and human services information technology systems, the railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and eligibility for entities to receive financial assistance from both the Iowa major events and tourism fund and the sports tourism infrastructure program, and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, passed on file.

IA-2025-SF2484.policyArea: administrative services department, agriculture and land stewardship department, appropriations
IA-2025-SF2484.aiSummary: This Iowa law makes money available for several state funds and projects in fiscal year 2026-2027. It includes funding for road and building work, water quality programs, farm fertilizer planning tools, and tourism-related funds. It also changes who can get some kinds of financial help, including regional sports authority districts and groups tied to major events, tourism, and sports tourism. The governor signed the bill but vetoed one part that would have limited some large health and human services technology contracts.

IA-2025-SF2220.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa statewide assessment of student progress and programs for gifted and talented children, and by requiring school districts to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and implement procedures for subject acceleration and whole-grade acceleration, and including applicability provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Message from House, with amendment S-5132.
Read first time, referred to Education.

IA-2025-SF2220.policyArea: children, education, gifted and talented education
IA-2025-SF2220.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa school rules for student testing, gifted and talented programs, advanced math, and course acceleration. It requires school districts to set up clearer ways to find and serve gifted and talented children, build an advanced math path, and create rules for subject and whole-grade acceleration and for automatic placement into more advanced classes for some students. It also says the state cost of these new rules must be paid from school foundation aid sent to districts.

IA-2025-HF2711.title: A bill for an act relating to state policies and programs with race or gender requirements.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.
Committee report, recommending amendment and passage.
Read first time, referred to Judiciary.

IA-2025-HF2711.policyArea: affirmative action, citizenship, colleges and universities
IA-2025-HF2711.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa rules on state programs and jobs that use race or gender-based requirements. It keeps equal-opportunity rules for state agencies, the regents, school districts, area education agencies, and community colleges, and it directs them to use affirmative action steps, training, reporting, and contract rules tied to Iowa-based businesses. It also gives the Department of Administrative Services and the Board of Regents duties to oversee these efforts and report on them.

IA-2025-HF2591.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa rules for open enrollment, student transfers, and school sports eligibility. It lets eighth graders join certain school sports contests on the same basis as high school students, and it sets new waiting periods for some students in grades 9 through 12 who transfer or use open enrollment before they can play varsity sports. The sports rule for eighth graders and the emergency rule steps took effect when the law was enacted, and the other changes took effect on August 1, 2026.

IA-2025-HF2531.title: A bill for an act relating to interests in minerals owned by counties and cities, and including effective date provisions.

House concurred in Senate amendment H-8478.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

Amendment H-8048 to amendment H-8033 filed, adopted.
Read first time, referred to Local Government.

IA-2025-HF2531.aiSummary: The law changes how counties and cities handle mineral interests under land. In most cases, they must give those mineral interests to the surface owner at no cost, with deadlines for older and newly acquired interests. It also changes rules for mineral taxes, tax sales, and when a coal mineral interest is treated as active or abandoned.

IA-2025-HF1028.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of management, and including effective date and applicability provisions.

IA-2025-HF1028.aiSummary: Now that it is law, this act changes several rules for the Iowa Department of Management. It lets the department move money between agencies under set limits, changes how the technology reinvestment fund is used and reported on, and gives it yearly funding for that fund. It also updates background check rules for some workers and bars certain contract terms, like ones that make the department take on another person's debt or let another party change terms on its own.

IA-2025-SF2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the excise tax on certain ethanol blended gasoline purchased exclusively for use in an implement of husbandry used in agricultural production.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, referred to Ways and Means.
Introduced, placed on Ways and Means calendar.

IA-2025-SF2493.aiSummary: This law exempts some ethanol-blended gasoline from Iowa’s excise tax when it is bought for use only in an implement of husbandry used in farm production. Buyers must use a state exemption certificate, and suppliers must keep it for at least three years. If the fuel is later used in a nonexempt way, the buyer must pay the tax directly to the state.

IA-2025-HF2678.title: A bill for an act providing for certain persons acting under the jurisdiction of the secretary of state, including by providing for information from required filings, and the administrative dissolution of certain entities, and making penalties applicable.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, attached to SF 2402.
Amendment H-8318 to amendment H-8123 filed, adopted.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

IA-2025-HF2678.aiSummary: The law changes filing rules for partnerships and limited partnerships with the Iowa secretary of state. It lets a person file a sworn statement if their name, address, or email was used without permission, and the secretary of state can remove that information with no fee. It also lets the secretary of state require some filings to be sent by mail or in person when there is credible information they may be fraudulent or used for an unlawful purpose, and it allows written questions to be sent to a partnership in those cases.

IA-2025-HF917.title: A bill for an act relating to civil liability actions against motocross facilities.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
House concurred in Senate amendment H-8262.
Committee report, recommending amendment and passage.
Read first time, referred to Judiciary.
Subcommittee: Behn, Johnson, R. and Meyer, A.

IA-2025-HF917.aiSummary: As law, this measure creates rules on lawsuits against motocross facilities in Iowa. It says a facility is not liable for injuries or death from the normal risks of motocross, like rider error, bad weather, animals, or remote locations without medical care. It also keeps liability in place for intentional harm, negligence, unsafe gear, or failing to use proper care, and it requires warning signs at the facility.
